about: MUTATING — delete ONE cluster object THE TREE ALREADY PROVES IS UNDECLARED, and nothing else (infra/forge/delete-orphan-object.sh). The converge applies infra/cluster/manifests with no --prune, so deleting a manifest removes the DECLARATION and leaves the OBJECT running; until this verb the only way to clear one was a human typing `kubectl -n boss delete svc <name>`, which blocked a gated-green car for nine days (backlog a139d5bb). THE AUTHORITY IS DERIVED, NOT GRANTED — and that is the whole design: there is deliberately NO general `kubectl delete` verb, because 'delete any object by name' hands an agent namespace-wide destruction through an audited door, which is worse than no door (CLAUDE.md: reads and bounded reclaims are mechanical, destructive-by-policy actions are not). Instead the script re-runs, at call time, the ONE definition of what is orphaned — infra/cluster/undeclared-objects.sh, the same computation the orphan lint reports from — and acts only if that computation NAMES the object it was given, using the kind/namespace/name from the derivation's own output rather than from the packet's string. Five bounds, each refusing loudly and by name: the argument's shape (re-checked in the script, not only here); the manifests directory must be CLEAN IN GIT, so the declaration set is reviewed content and a rename in progress can never be eligible (and EVERY git read drops to the checkout's owner, read off the directory with stat — the runner executes verbs as root, git refuses to read a clone it does not own, and the first live run refused a real checkout as 'not a git checkout' for exactly that reason, ops-request c9877f75; same as_owner shape as infra/gcp/boss-gcp-converge.sh); the derivation must say undeclared (it refuses a declared object, a namespace the tree does not own, a kind the tree declares nothing of, an excluded kind, an exempt object, a controller-owned object, an object that is not live — and says CANNOT ANSWER, never 'undeclared', when a credential cannot list the pair or a manifest will not parse); the verb's own KIND FLOOR, narrower than the derivation's scope (Service, ConfigMap, Deployment, CronJob, Job — kinds a manifest reapply restores completely; PVC/StatefulSet are bytes, Secret and ServiceAccount are credentials, Role/RoleBinding are privileges, and all of those stay a named human step); and CAPTURE BEFORE DELETE — the object's YAML is printed onto this packet first, because a deleted object cannot be read back. `--dry-run` runs every bound and deletes nothing, so the verb is exercisable through the runner without acting. Its own timeout: the derivation parses every manifest with kubectl, which exceeds the runner's 30s default. Authorized by David 2026-09-10 ('let's make sure any cars that are blocked on my manual intervention get a job to create an agent-usable mechanism'), same explicit per-verb process as reclaim-disk / rollback-to / converge / publish-github-pr — a precedent for the PROCESS, not a loosened default.
